entry.title: When I Feel Like I Can't Do It Anymore
entry.summary: Sometimes, faith means continuing even when you feel tired. There are days when I feel like I've reached my limit. I have schoolwork waiting for me, deadlines getting closer, and…
entry.content:
Sometimes, faith means continuing even when you feel tired.

There are days when I feel like I've reached my limit.

I have schoolwork waiting for me, deadlines getting closer, and lessons that I still don't completely understand. Sometimes I sit in front of my laptop and wonder how I'm going to finish everything.

As a BSIT student, there are times when programming feels frustrating.

One error turns into another.

Something that should have taken an hour takes the whole day.

And after trying again and again, I sometimes just want to give up.

It's Okay to Be Tired

I've learned that being tired doesn't mean I'm weak.

There are days when I don't feel motivated.

There are days when I make mistakes.

There are days when I don't accomplish everything I planned.

And that's okay.

I don't have to be strong every second.

I can rest.

I can cry.

I can admit that something is difficult.

And I can bring that feeling to God.

“I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.”
— Philippians 4:13

This verse reminds me that my strength doesn't have to come entirely from myself.

When My Own Strength Isn't Enough

Sometimes I try to solve everything on my own.

I keep pushing myself because I think I should be able to handle everything.

But eventually, I realize that I need God.

I need His wisdom when I don't know what to do.

I need His peace when I'm anxious.

I need His strength when I'm exhausted.

And I need His reminder that one difficult day doesn't mean I've failed.

I Can Start Again Tomorrow

Maybe I don't have to finish everything tonight.

Maybe I just need to finish what I can.

Maybe I need to close my laptop, say a prayer, get some rest, and try again tomorrow.

Starting again isn't failure.

Sometimes, starting again is courage.

College is teaching me more than just programming and technology.

It's teaching me patience.

It's teaching me discipline.

It's teaching me how to handle failure.

And most importantly, it's teaching me how much I need God.

Keep Going

I don't know exactly how difficult the road ahead will be.

There will probably be more assignments, more exams, more difficult programs, and more moments when I question myself.

But I don't want fear to be the reason I stop.

I want to keep going.

Not because I know I can handle everything by myself, but because I know I can bring everything to God.

When I feel like I can't do it anymore, I'll remind myself:

I can rest, but I don't have to give up.

I can take one more step.

I can try one more time.

I can pray one more prayer.

And tomorrow, I can begin again.

God is still with me—even on the days when I don't feel strong. 🤍

entry.title: Finding God in the Little Things
entry.summary:
Sometimes, His blessings are hidden in the ordinary.

College life can make me focus so much on what I still need to accomplish that I forget to notice what I already have.

I think about the next assignment.

The next exam.

The next deadline.

The next problem I need to solve.

Sometimes, I'm so focused on getting through the day that I forget to stop and be thankful.

But recently, I've been learning that God's goodness isn't always found in huge, life-changing moments.

Sometimes, it's found in the little things.

A Simple Day Can Still Be a Blessing

A quiet morning.

A good meal after a long day.

A friend who makes me laugh when I'm stressed.

A professor who explains something until I finally understand it.

A program that finally works after hours of debugging.

A few minutes of peace before going to sleep.

These things may seem small, but they remind me that there is still so much to be thankful for.

“This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.”
— Psalm 118:24

Every day doesn't have to be perfect for it to be a gift.

When I'm Too Focused on What's Missing

Sometimes, I compare my life to other people.

I see people who seem to have everything figured out.

Someone is already achieving something I want.

Someone seems more confident.

Someone seems further ahead.

And without realizing it, I start thinking about everything I don't have.

But comparison makes it easy to overlook God's blessings in my own life.

I have my own journey.

My own pace.

My own lessons.

And I believe God has a purpose for each season.

Thank You, Lord

So today, I want to pause and simply say:

Thank You, Lord.

Thank You for giving me another day.

Thank You for the strength to continue studying even when I'm tired.

Thank You for the people who encourage me.

Thank You for the opportunities I have.

Thank You for the lessons that challenge me.

Thank You even for the difficult moments that are teaching me to become stronger.

And thank You for staying with me through all of it.

Learning to Notice

I'm still learning how to slow down.

I'm still learning how to appreciate what I have instead of constantly worrying about what comes next.

Maybe God's blessings aren't always loud.

Maybe sometimes they're quiet.

Maybe they're hidden inside ordinary moments that I would normally overlook.

So I want to start paying more attention.

To the little joys.

The small victories.

The peaceful moments.

The answered prayers.

And even the challenges that help me grow.

Because when I look closely, I realize that God has been there all along.

In the big moments.
In the difficult moments.
And especially in the little ones. 🤍

A simple meal.

A peaceful moment.

A friend checking up on me.

A good conversation.

Finally understanding a difficult lesson.

Even getting home safely after a long day.

These ordinary moments may not seem significant, but they are reminders that God's goodness is present even in the simplest parts of my life.

Sometimes, I think I'm waiting for a big blessing before I can truly be grateful. But maybe gratitude begins with recognizing the blessings that are already here.

“This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.”
— Psalm 118:24

College has taught me that life won't always go according to my plans. There will be stressful deadlines, difficult subjects, unanswered questions, and moments when I feel like I'm falling behind.

But I'm learning that I don't have to have everything figured out.

I can simply take one day at a time.

And in every ordinary day, I can choose to notice God's goodness.

entry.title: When God Feels Silent
entry.summary: I learned to trust God even when I don't understand what He's doing. There are moments in life when I pray and wait for an answer. I ask God for…
entry.content:
I learned to trust God even when I don't understand what He's doing.

There are moments in life when I pray and wait for an answer.

I ask God for guidance. I ask Him to help me with my problems, my studies, my future, and the things that worry me.

But sometimes, nothing seems to change.

The problem is still there.

The deadline is still coming.

The answer I'm waiting for hasn't arrived.

And I start wondering:

“Lord, are You listening?”

The Silence Can Be Difficult

I think one of the hardest parts of faith is waiting.

It's easy to trust God when everything is going according to plan.

It's harder when I'm praying about something and the situation doesn't seem to change.

As a student, I sometimes want immediate answers. I want to know whether I'm making the right decisions. I want to know where my degree will take me and what my future will look like.

But God doesn't always give me the answer immediately.

And I'm learning that silence doesn't necessarily mean absence.

Maybe God Is Teaching Me to Wait

Sometimes, I think God is doing something even when I can't see it yet.

Maybe the waiting is teaching me patience.

Maybe the uncertainty is teaching me trust.

Maybe the difficult season is teaching me to depend on Him instead of depending completely on myself.

“Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart.”
— Psalm 27:14

Waiting isn't easy.

But I'm learning that I don't have to understand everything to trust God.

My Future Is Still Unclear

I don't know exactly where my BSIT journey will take me.

I don't know what job I'll have after graduation.

I don't know what opportunities will come my way.

There are so many things about the future that I cannot see.

But maybe that's okay.

If I already knew everything that would happen, I wouldn't need faith.

So instead of constantly asking God to show me the entire road, I'm learning to ask Him to guide my next step.

Just the next step.

Still Here

Even on days when I feel like God is quiet, I want to remember everything He has already brought me through.

The prayers He has answered.

The doors He has opened.

The strength He gave me when I thought I couldn't continue.

The people He placed in my life.

The little blessings I sometimes forget to notice.

Maybe God isn't always silent.

Maybe sometimes I'm simply being asked to slow down enough to notice Him.

So I'll keep praying.

I'll keep studying.

I'll keep trying.

I'll keep trusting.

And even when I don't know what comes next, I'll continue walking forward with God.

I may not see the whole path, but I know who I'm walking with. 🤍

entry.title: When College Feels Too Heavy
entry.summary: Learning to pause, pray, and trust God in the middle of the pressure. There are days when college feels heavier than usual. As a BSIT student, I sometimes find myself…
entry.content:
Learning to pause, pray, and trust God in the middle of the pressure.

There are days when college feels heavier than usual.

As a BSIT student, I sometimes find myself staring at my laptop for hours, trying to understand a program that refuses to work. There are activities to finish, lessons to study, deadlines to remember, and exams waiting around the corner.

Sometimes, I start thinking:

“Kaya ko pa ba?”

I know I'm supposed to keep going, but there are moments when I feel completely exhausted.

When I Don't Know What to Do

I've learned that one of the hardest parts of being a student isn't always the workload.

Sometimes, it's the fear that comes with it.

The fear of failing.

The fear of disappointing myself.

The fear that maybe I'm not good enough.

And when those thoughts become too loud, I try to remind myself to stop for a moment.

To breathe.

To pray.

I don't always have a long prayer. Sometimes it's simply:

“Lord, please help me get through this.”

And somehow, saying those words reminds me that I don't have to carry everything alone.

God Doesn't Promise an Easy Life

Being a Christian doesn't mean that I won't struggle.

There will still be difficult subjects, stressful deadlines, mistakes, and days when I don't feel motivated.

But I believe God can meet me even in those ordinary and difficult moments.

“Cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee.”
— Psalm 55:22

I love the reminder that I can bring my burdens to God.

I don't have to pretend that everything is okay when it isn't.

I can tell Him that I'm tired.

I can tell Him that I'm scared.

I can tell Him that I don't understand.

And I can trust Him with the things I cannot control.

One Step at a Time

Sometimes I think too far ahead.

I worry about graduating.

I worry about my career.

I worry about whether I'll become the person I hope to be.

But maybe I don't need to figure everything out today.

Today, I just need to do what I can.

Finish the assignment.

Study the lesson.

Fix the code.

Get some rest.

Pray.

Then do it again tomorrow.

I am slowly learning that progress doesn't always look big. Sometimes, progress is simply choosing not to give up.

If You're Struggling Too

If you're also a student who feels tired, overwhelmed, or uncertain about the future, I hope you remember this:

You don't have to have everything figured out right now.

Your current struggle is only one part of your story.

Keep doing your part, but don't forget to give your worries to God.

Study hard.

Pray harder.

Rest when you need to.

And keep going.

Because maybe the season you're struggling through today is preparing you for something you cannot see yet.

One day at a time.
One prayer at a time.
One line of code at a time.

I'm still learning.

I'm still struggling.

I'm still growing.

But I'm not walking alone. 🤍

entry.title: Walking With God Through College
entry.summary: A Christian student's journey through pressure, purpose, and faith. College was something I looked forward to, but I don't think I fully understood how challenging it would be. As a…
entry.content:
A Christian student's journey through pressure, purpose, and faith.

College was something I looked forward to, but I don't think I fully understood how challenging it would be.

As a BSIT student, there are days when school feels overwhelming. There are programming activities that don't work no matter how many times I try to fix them, deadlines that seem to come all at once, exams to prepare for, and moments when I wonder if I'm really capable of doing all of this.

Sometimes, I get tired.

Sometimes, I feel pressured.

And sometimes, I question whether I'm good enough.

But somewhere between the deadlines, sleepless nights, and stressful days, I've been learning something important:

I don't have to go through college alone.

When I Feel Like Giving Up

There are moments when I just want to stop for a while.

When a program doesn't work, when I don't understand a lesson, or when I feel like everyone else is doing better than me, it's easy to become discouraged.

But I've slowly learned to bring those feelings to God.

I may not always know what to do next, but I can pray.

I may not have all the answers, but I can trust Him.

“Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.”
— Proverbs 16:3

This verse reminds me that my efforts matter, but I don't have to carry everything by myself.

Faith and My Studies

Being a Christian doesn't mean that college suddenly becomes easy.

I still have to study.

I still have to practice programming.

I still have to submit requirements and prepare for exams.

Faith doesn't replace hard work. Instead, it gives me a reason to keep going when the work becomes difficult.

Before an exam, I can pray.

Before starting an assignment, I can ask God for wisdom.

When I make mistakes, I can remind myself that one failure doesn't define me.

And when something finally works after hours of frustration, I can thank Him for giving me the strength to keep trying.

Learning to Trust God's Timing

One of the hardest things I'm learning is that my plans aren't always God's plans.

Sometimes I want things to happen immediately.

I want to know where my degree will take me.

I want to know what my future career will look like.

I want to know whether all the effort I'm putting into my studies will eventually be worth it.

But I am learning to take things one day at a time.

I don't need to know everything about my future to trust the One who already knows it.

“For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD...”
— Jeremiah 29:11

Still Learning, Still Growing

I'm not writing this because I have everything figured out.

I don't.

I'm still a student. I'm still learning programming, learning how to handle pressure, learning how to manage my time, and most importantly, learning how to grow in my relationship with God.

There will probably be more difficult semesters.

More difficult subjects.

More moments of doubt.

More nights when I feel exhausted.

But I hope that through all of them, I remember that God is still with me.

My degree is part of my journey, but it isn't my entire identity.

Before I am a BSIT student, I am someone who is learning to walk with Christ.

And whatever happens next, I want to keep moving forward with Him.

One assignment at a time.
One challenge at a time.
One prayer at a time.

And one day, I hope I can look back and say:

“God was with me through it all.” 🤍
